title: Towards 2+1D quantum electrodynamics on a cold-atom quantum simulator
abstract: We present a feasible cold-atom quantum simulator of a (2+1)-dimensional U(1) lattice gauge theory with expanded gauge-field parameters that exceed previous experimental limitations. The approach leverages quantum Zeno dynamics to preserve gauge constraints while mapping the theory onto a single-species Bose-Hubbard model in a tilted optical superlattice, achievable with existing laboratory equipment. We validate our design using simulations demonstrating faithful evolution of the target gauge theory and robust preservation of the gauge constraints, marking meaningful progress toward exploring quantum electrodynamics phenomena in controlled experimental settings.
key_claims: Proposes cold-atom implementation of (2+1)D U(1) lattice gauge theory
Quantum Zeno dynamics preserves gauge constraints without active correction
Maps to Bose-Hubbard model in tilted optical superlattice -- existing hardware compatible
Extends prior 1+1D Schwinger-model results to higher dimensions
Relevant to worldline simulation in 2+1D spacetime
